_comment: An empty beach out of season. The temptation with a beach is to make it a holiday; this one is deliberately not. Flat overcast, nobody else, everything packed away -- a family walk in October, which is the version people actually have on tape. DE-NATIONALISED 2026-08-29: this was a Baltic beach and its strongest details (Strandkorb, groyne, marram dune) were northern-European landmarks. The specificity did not go, it MOVED -- from country to ERA. A shuttered kiosk and a chained bin say out-of-season anywhere on earth; a thermos, a paper map and a disposable camera say 2003 anywhere on earth. That swap is the whole rule for this catalog now.
label: The beach, out of season

prompt._comment: The kiosk with its shutters down is the detail that carries this preset -- it says the season is over without naming a coast, and it exists on every coastline in the world. One line of footprints does the same work the empty beach chairs used to: somebody is here, and nobody else is.
prompt.scene: a wide empty beach out of season, wet packed sand holding a single line of footprints, a shuttered kiosk with its awning rolled up and padlocked, stacked plastic beach loungers under a weighted tarpaulin, a litter bin chained to its post
prompt.light: flat overcast with no shadow at all, the water and the sky nearly the same grey, the sand slightly brighter than both
prompt.lens: wide and low with a lot of sky, the horizon almost straight across the frame
prompt.framing: waist-up against the empty sand, the shuttered kiosk small over one shoulder
prompt._moment: What is HAPPENING, not what is in frame. A brief with no action in it is a portrait brief, and the model answers it with a portrait -- squared to the camera, arms hanging, waiting. Somebody caught halfway through something ordinary is what a real snapshot looks like.
prompt.moment: walking back up the sand and only just noticing the camera, one arm still out for balance
prompt.eraProps: a metal thermos flask, a fold-out paper map weighted down with a stone, a disposable camera with a wind-on wheel, a portable radio with a telescopic aerial

motionHint: the water moves in slow flat lines up the sand, the loose corner of the tarpaulin lifts and snaps, and the padlock swings against the shutter

lookOverride._comment: The coldest and flattest thing in the menu. Saturation well down, warmth backed almost out (remember bm negative = yellow, so raising cbBlueMid towards zero cools it), halation nearly off because a flat overcast sky has no specular highlight to halate, and the least grain of any preset because there is nothing here for it to hide in.

ambience._comment: Surf and onshore wind. The swell is the waves: 0.18 Hz is about one every five and a half seconds, which is what the preset means by "slow flat lines up the sand". Lowpassed hard because a camcorder mic in wind has no top end left.
